claims.text: The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase disordered BCC alloy based on Mo, Nb, Ta, W, and V.
Approximately 5 at% Al will be added to the baseline alloy.
Adding approximately 5 at% Al will induce fine, dispersed, ordered B2 precipitates within the BCC matrix.
The B2 precipitates will hinder dislocation motion.
The precipitates will remain effective obstacles at elevated temperature, where diffusion and dislocation climb are more active.
Precipitate strengthening will increase high-temperature mechanical strength.
The Al-modified alloy will have higher yield strength at 800°C than the baseline alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will exhibit slower creep at 800°C than the baseline alloy.
A small, controlled precipitate volume fraction will prevent substantial impairment of room-temperature ductility.
The Al-modified alloy will have negligible changes in room-temperature mechanical performance relative to the baseline.
The controlled Al addition and small precipitate volume fraction will limit the overall density change.
The Al-modified alloy will have only a minimal increase in density relative to the baseline.
Maintaining the Al concentration near 5 at% is necessary for the proposed beneficial effect.
Al concentrations above approximately 5 at% may cause precipitate coarsening or embrittlement.
Al concentrations below approximately 5 at% may produce an insufficient precipitate volume fraction.
The proposed performance benefit will taper off at temperatures significantly above 800°C.
High-temperature performance will be evaluated by tensile and constant-load creep testing at 800°C.
Room-temperature performance will be evaluated using quasi-static tensile testing.
